reviews.text: Very professional and caring, and even though it was my first time at the emergency vet and my cat was hospitalized for three days, it's clear they know what they're doing and they have a real love for cats. I highly recommend them.

Kon and I are so grateful that you've given us more time together. Thank you to Elisa and Elena for doing everything possible! And thank you to the team for taking such good care of him!
Thank you from the bottom of our hearts 🙏 …

If you truly love your cats, don't bring them here unless you enjoy spending money and want to be misinformed. I had to call two days later to get the tests done so he could be treated at another hospital.

They said he didn't have anything serious, but it turns out my boy had an infection and was suffering.

I'm giving him two stars because the vet, Angie, who treated us, was incredibly sweet and caring with my baby. I'm not giving you the other two stars because your service, both in terms of information and management, leaves much to be desired. If I'm bringing in a sick animal, the last thing I need is the lack of empathy from the staff at the counter. People already have enough to deal with because of their sick pets.

Seriously, please show a little consideration when dealing with customers. You wouldn't find that kind of rudeness even at Zara.

Best regards and a hug for Angie!

The description this clinic gives of itself doesn't always match reality. I took a kitten from my colony who was seriously ill (he had a severe infection due to a broken tooth), and everything was going well until they asked if he was vaccinated. When I said no, the girl's face changed drastically, and she became harsh and serious. She told me she couldn't take him, that the "infectious" area was full and there was no room for my kitten, and that I should go to another clinic nearby. It was a real blow. The worst part was the cheap and poorly thought-out excuse she gave me: that a girl from the colony had brought her many cats that very afternoon, and the infectious area was full. Even she doesn't believe that. I'm from a colony, and it's literally impossible for us to bring that many cats in a single afternoon. Our kitten is already well thanks to another clinic that has a better rating than yours. And the mind of the girl who attended to me was infectious! Absolutely awful! I will never return to your clinic, which is located way out in the boonies! Feline clinic, a clinic to forget!!!! Goodbye forever!!!!!!! Disrespecting colony kittens. Shameful! You're veterinary students. You're not real veterinarians. You wish!!! Your advertising is an absolute eyesore.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND this clinic at all, and even less so with Dra. Marta Maceda as the responsible veterinarian.

I carefully chose this clinic for the ongoing monitoring of my two cats with early-stage chronic kidney disease, precisely because this condition requires proper checkups and a long-term relationship of trust with the veterinarian. The result was exactly the opposite: an accumulation of errors that speak for themselves:

- Blood draw: two tubes were taken from one of the cats, and neither turned out valid (haemolysis was cited as the cause). This cat has had blood tests for years and this had never happened before.

- Urinalysis: the sample was not processed immediately, it was sent elsewhere, and the result only arrived the next day. I was told in writing that there were no crystals - the official IDEXX lab report showed 5-15 struvite crystals per field. In addition, for the first time in this cat's life, blood appeared in the urine sample, something that had never happened before. The veterinarian herself acknowledged in writing that this could artificially distort the UPC result. Everything points to an incorrectly performed sample collection. How can I trust an analysis like this, and why should I have to pay for it?

- Confusion between renal calcifications and stones in the reports, and contradictory treatment recommendations within the same document.

- A systematic refusal to clearly answer specific technical questions I raised repeatedly in writing.

Despite all this documented evidence, the clinic has refused to refund the cost of the urinalysis. At no point throughout this process did I receive an apology or any acknowledgment of the mistakes made - only a distant attitude and denial of obvious facts.

I consider that Dra. Marta Maceda does not offer the level of competence required for the ongoing management of chronic conditions, and I do not recommend her at all as the veterinarian responsible for a case.
Veterinary clinic dedicated exclusively to cats. Excellent care and dedication.
They don't care about animals, only money.

I recently moved to the area and was recommended Clínica Felina (Feline Clinic). I couldn't be happier! They have a fantastic team and are far from trying to charge you for anything you don't really need. They are kind, always have a smile, and are happy to answer your questions and more. My little one and I are so grateful to have found them ❤️✨🫂

A high level of professionalism.
From the moment they attended to us, they reviewed the reports and analyses we provided and gave us a quote for the tests and treatment they would perform.
They kept us informed at all times about our pet's progress and confirmed that the treatment was the right one. Our kitten was back home within 48 hours.
Thank you so much for your attention and for the pampering and care you gave our pet.
A terrible clinic

Our experience with Clínica Felina Barcelona has been excellent, and we are immensely grateful to them.

We came to them after going through a very uncertain time with our cat and having spent a lot of money at another veterinary clinic without getting a clear diagnosis or really knowing what was wrong with him, watching his life slip away.

Here, Dr. Diego saw us and identified a possible diagnosis from the very first moment. From there, they carried out the necessary tests to confirm it, and we were able to quickly begin the appropriate treatment. Thanks to this, we were able to save our cat's life and see him recover.

Since then, we continue to trust them for our veterinary care. It's very clear that they specialize in felines: they know how to treat and handle them, something that, as cat owners, we especially appreciate. Furthermore, the entire team is friendly, attentive, professional, and inspires a lot of confidence.

We also feel it's important to mention that the prices are reasonable and in line with the care and treatments provided, something we value even more after our previous experience.

We are incredibly grateful to Dr. Diego and the entire team for taking care of our cat when he needed it most and for continuing to do so to this day.

We highly recommend them. 🐾
Many thanks for everything!
I went for a check-up and everything was great, clear explanations.

Highly recommended if you're unsure where to take your cats for their annual checkups, tests, or emergencies.

Excellent service: always attentive, kind, and very empathetic. It's the clinic for both of my cats, and they've always been treated with great care.

It's fantastic that they're open 24 hours. I called once, and they answered even though it was very late at night.

After almost two years since the loss of my cat on August 27, 2024, I've finally found the strength to write this review and share our experience at this clinic.

Unfortunately, our experience was very negative. Throughout the entire process, we incurred a significant financial outlay, yet at no point did I feel we received a clear and definitive explanation of what was happening to our cat. I endured the process with immense anguish and the feeling of not truly understanding the diagnosis or the direction of the treatment.

What hurts me the most is that, while we continued to believe they could help him, my cat continued to suffer, and the process dragged on until he finally had to be sedated. To this day, I still believe the situation could have been handled differently, prioritizing his well-being more clearly and avoiding prolonging his suffering.

Furthermore, throughout the entire process, I had a very unpleasant feeling that the financial aspect played an undue role in how the case was managed.

I would also like to emphasize that, personally, I perceived a very cold attitude during a time that was extremely painful for us. In a situation like this, in addition to veterinary care, I believe that empathy, communication, and the ability to know when to prioritize the animal's well-being are fundamental.

I fully understand that there are complex cases and that it's not always possible to arrive at a simple or immediate diagnosis. My criticism doesn't stem from expecting a veterinarian to be able to resolve any situation, but rather from how we experienced the entire process: a lack of clarity, a constant feeling of uncertainty, a very high financial cost, and, above all, the perception that our animal's suffering was being prolonged.
Professional and friendly, always a good experience.

I'm very unhappy with this clinic. The veterinarians who treat you, in my opinion, lack genuine interest and professionalism. It seems like they've just finished painting their nails and intend to continue doing so after treating your cat. It's obvious the clinic isn't theirs, that they're just on the payroll and don't care about the animal's health. In 2017, I took my kitten there because she had kidney problems, and at the end of the visit, I mentioned that her pupils were dilated. Instead of suggesting it might be hypertension, the veterinarian said she didn't know what it was and that if it persisted, she would give me the contact information for an ophthalmologist. My kitten ended up going blind, most likely due to kidney failure. Recently, I took my kitten back to the clinic, trusting them again. How naive and foolish of me! This time, the veterinarian told me that if the kitten was nervous in the carrier, I should let him down. So I did, and my cat contracted rhinotracheitis and infected another of my cats. I complained and they told me they would refund the visit fee, but I'm still waiting. I won't be going back. There's terrible organization. I don't know what's really going on, but I saw the waiting room empty, which must mean something, and this clinic was always packed when it first opened. It's a shame. Are the managers incapable of managing their employees? Or are they not veterinarians themselves and don't really know what happened when problems arise? I don't know... but it's a shame. The manager was very kind when I filed my complaint, but in the end, she didn't refund my money for the inconvenience caused.

In our case, the veterinarian caring for Lucky is Elena. I can't thank her enough for her dedication, kindness, and professionalism. We are very happy with her work, and she answers any questions or concerns we have immediately. Thank you so much for your care of Lucky and us. I wholeheartedly recommend this clinic if you need veterinary help for your feline friend. You'll have the utmost professionalism at your side.
Excellent service and very professional.

I'd give them -1000 if it wouldn't let me! My cat was terminally ill, with kidney failure and cancer, 17 years old—you only had to look at him to see it. My usual clinic didn't have availability for euthanasia (urgent), but they did… but not before making a profit. I understand they charge for the emergency visit and the euthanasia plus cremation, but demanding tests and analyses (as they told me over the phone) is outrageous. If they even saw the cat, they should be ashamed… otherwise, they couldn't euthanize him! Thanks to Hospital Veterinari Montjuic at Calle Mexic 30 (it's nearby), for being humane, caring, and not wanting to profit from the suffering of a 17-year-old cat who died in a few hours… AWFUL! I hope fate puts you in your place; humanity and humility are not characteristics of your clinic.

After a bad experience at another veterinary hospital, my veterinarian recommended this clinic. I must say that the treatment from the veterinary staff and assistants was excellent every time I visited, including two hospitalizations. The staff was very attentive, caring, and empathetic. Unfortunately, my pet had to undergo emergency surgery with a poor prognosis, but I felt supported and guided throughout the entire process. If I needed to go again, I would return without hesitation. Thank you all for your dedication and great work. Thank you.

Very clean, very professional, very friendly.

I will come again.

On Christmas Day (2025) my cat Antonio became fatal. A brutal urinary obstruction that got worse at times. His usual (ex-)veterinarian wouldn't answer the phone and I called the feline clinic. They attended to me immediately and even though there were no Christmas presents that year, they saved him. I must say that they gave me several treatment options and the equivalent prices, but with the most reasonable option we were able to solve the problem. The doctor was great, and I felt well taken care of, without any pressure to go for the most expensive treatment. Needless to say, when we need it, we already know directly where to go! Thank you very much for everything! ❤️‍🩹

I have no words to express my gratitude for everything you did for my Ash Jamoncito. Thank you for caring for him with so much love until the very end and for the moral support you gave me. Without a doubt, I will take my other feline children to you for care. "In the midst of the profound sorrow of Ash Jamoncito's passing, I am comforted knowing that he was in the best hands. Thank you for your empathy, your professionalism, and for supporting us until the very end. You have my complete trust in the care of my other cats."
A very good clinic; they take care of my cats there and provide excellent service. Very friendly and attentive to clients; I highly recommend them.
Very good service. A little expensive.

Wonderful experience in what can be a veterinary visit with a cat that has an extremely bad time with handling and in the context that going to the vet is because something is not going quite right.
They were able to give us an appointment scheduled for the same week and the vet Marta attended to us.

Despite being one of those guardians who ask everything, who suffer for everything and who can be a bit heavy (🙏🏼), we felt listened to and accompanied at all times.

The kitten who is only 10 months old and has a long veterinary history, does not let herself be touched and gets VERY angry, but when she woke up from the sedation we were surprised to see her so “comfortable” in the consultation, even being able to choose the carrier if she felt threatened. Which for us has a lot of value for what it implies (good handling to sedate her and explore despite being a Spicy Tricolor 🌶️🌶️)

We hope not to have to step foot in a vet for a long time but we definitely know where we have to go!!
Fantastic streaks! Very decisive

Delighted with the clinic's service and, of course, with the professionalism of the veterinarian who treated us, Elena. Our cat Nemo (hopefully it won't be long before he's gone) will always be back whenever we need him. Thank you to the clinic and all the staff.

I've always trusted them to care for my cats. Two of them are no longer with us, and thanks to their team, they were able to get through that time in the best possible way, with respect and support.
The 24-hour service is a huge plus: in emergency situations, knowing they're there at any time provides immense peace of mind. The care is personal, with highly individualized follow-up and, above all, great professionalism. You truly feel your pet is in the best hands.
I want to especially highlight Elisa, their oncologist (although she's far more knowledgeable than just her specialty), and the rest of the team, who have always been impeccable. I continue to go to them and wholeheartedly recommend them to anyone who has a cat and wants to give the best possible care to a member of the family.

I've been taking my two cats (Rollo and Honey) to CFB for many years, and I couldn't be happier with the care they receive. Diego, in particular, is a fantastic professional, incredibly knowledgeable, and it's clear he's passionate about them. Whenever we've had an emergency, we've gone there without hesitation, and they've treated us wonderfully.

My sincerest thanks to him and the entire CFB team; you deserve all the positive feedback you've received.

Thank you so much.

Terrible experience. All they care about is making as much money as possible. I took my cat in because she had eaten plants and vomited immediately. I went simply to put my mind at ease, as she wasn't showing any signs of illness. The moment I walked in, they told me that she would most likely DIE, literally, without even running a SINGLE TEST first.

The way they communicated this was so insensitive that I was frozen with shock. And the second they told me that, they were already quoting me 700 euros to "see if they could save her." They completely exploit your desperation to get you to pay (!!!!!!!)

I left her there, and when I returned, they had run more tests, including some that weren't included in the initial estimate… and, of course, they charged me for those too. My cat didn't show a single symptom or problem in the tests, but they still insisted I keep her for another day.

They never showed me the test results. How do I know if they were actually doing them?

I admitted her again, and when I went back the next day to pick her up (and pay the unnecessary exorbitant fee), they added even more tests that I did NOT authorize.

In short, the whole thing ended up costing me 1000 euros for absolutely nothing. And the feeling that my cat could die, communicated in such a cold way, is something I'll never forget.

This place should be shut down immediately! DO NOT TAKE YOUR CATS THERE!

Excellent professionals, there are specialists in different areas (feline diabetes, dentistry, etc.) who provide solutions to difficult problems, to treat, or to pathologies that are complicated to diagnose.

There are places you return to not because they're close, but because you trust them. For me, that place is Clínica Felina Barcelona.

It's actually the only vet I've taken my cats to since 2018. They've been with Lucius since he was a kitten, following his history, his personality, and his needs with invaluable consistency.

Lucius recently had surgery there, and it's not the first time I've trusted their team: they also cared for Kanye in 2023. In both cases, the experience was impeccable, but what truly makes the difference is something harder to find: genuine dedication and deeply respectful care for the animals… and for those of us who love them.

Even though I now live 200 km from Barcelona, ​​I still choose them. Because I know that there my cats are in the hands of professionals who not only know what they're doing, but do it with extraordinary sensitivity.

I want to give a special mention to Marta and Salva, always attentive, always there. Their email follow-up, their personal touch, and the way they support you during such delicate moments make everything a little easier and much more human.

It's not just a veterinary clinic. It's a place where you know they'll care for your pets as if they were their own. And that, for me, is everything.

The cat's well-being isn't their top priority. In my experience, they prioritize profit above all else, turning into a factory for churning out as many tests and treatments as possible (not always necessary, and sometimes at the expense of making the cat worse).
I took my cat in on Tuesday with blood work from Monday indicating very advanced kidney failure. The first thing they suggested was admission for further testing and fluid resuscitation. That's when the torture began. The tests and ultrasound confirmed the severity. After two days of treatment, they gave me my cat back. When I got home, the animal was almost dead, unable to stand or walk. After two hours, he was having trouble breathing, and we had to have him euthanized (at a different clinic, of course). I understand the severity of his condition, and my cat would have died anyway. But the torture wasn't necessary, like sedating him every day for a simple blood test (which greatly worsened his condition), prolonging his stay and treatment unnecessarily. THIS CLINIC, WHICH PRESENTS ITSELF AS SPECIAL FOR ITS TREATMENT OF CATS, DOESN'T MEET THE BASIC STANDARDS TO BE "READY OPTIMAL FOR CATS." On one day of admission, the cat was handled by more than six different people between 8 and 10 a.m. Four people... one feeds him, another examines him, another does blood work, another cleans the litter box... (with all the stress this causes a cat). A cat without strength, almost terminally ill, and they sedate him for a simple blood test every day... when it wasn't necessary... they keep them with The cat had a bowl of wet food, but it was already dry all day. He was in a cubicle smelling of litter box urine and food... knowing he was suffering from nausea. Knowing there was no solution, they performed another blood test under sedation and sent him home, saying he had improved and could stay for a few days. He died six hours after leaving the clinic.
They care more about making money than the cat's well-being. It's a testing factory with no empathy for the animal, least of all a cat.
I can't see my review. I went in to ask for information and the receptionist (Argentine) was very unpleasant and rude. I say "Argentine" because of her accent and because I don't know her name.
We took our cat Coco twice and the service was wonderful. The staff was incredibly attentive and provided excellent service.

I couldn't have found a better place to care for my cat. The staff were all amazing. The quality of service and the price were excellent. A special thank you to Marta, our veterinarian, for keeping us informed every step of the way. Thank you for everything; I will recommend them to everyone.

I'm not a client of the clinic, but this afternoon we found an injured cat near their clinic and went in to ask if we could bring it in to have it checked for a microchip. Not only did they say yes, but two women came out to help us catch it. It was difficult, but they finally managed to catch it and took it to be examined and to try to find its owners.

Thank you so much for not turning a blind eye and helping us, as we didn't know what to do!
Everything was great! Completely trustworthy
My experience was extremely positive, especially since Ofelia took such good care of my kitten Sia. They treat the kittens with professionalism and affection. Thank you!

I have been taking my cats to the Feline Clinic for many years and they have always been treated with professionalism, empathy and sensitivity. And the reception assistants are always very friendly. Thanks to the whole team for taking care of my kitties for so many years!

It's an excellent clinic. Very good service and facilities. I really appreciated that they let me go into the examination room while I waited for the vet so the cats could get used to it, leave their carriers, and not be so nervous. A top-notch place, highly recommended!

IT WAS MALIGNANT CANCER

I went to this clinic twice, thinking that since it specializes only in felines, they would be more careful and better prepared to treat my cats.

The first visit wasn't particularly bad. They prescribed one of my cats a very strong treatment that left him completely unconscious. While the treatment lasted, it seemed to work, but after it ended, everything got worse again.

The second time, I went because of a lump that looked very bad. The service was terrible from the start: they made us wait more than 40 minutes and moved us to a different room three times, once to a tiny room full of junk. My cat suffers terribly every time he leaves the house; he even injures himself inside his carrier due to the stress.

Finally, they saw us, but without giving us any clear explanations. They only said they didn't know what it could be and that they didn't see anything unusual. They pricked him twice to take samples, which caused the area to become even more damaged and the wound to worsen significantly.

Luckily, I decided to go to another vet, where they treated us with immense kindness and professionalism. Today we received the biopsy results: it was MALIGNANT CANCER.

I didn't want to write this review weeks ago, but honestly, I would have liked to have read something like this before deciding that this clinic would be our go-to vet.

PS: I posted this same review before and it was deleted; they even blocked me, claiming "sexual content." The attached photos showed exactly what you yourselves saw when you entered the clinic and chose to ignore. Shameful.

I want to express my deepest gratitude to Elisa, the veterinarian at the Barcelona Feline Center, for everything she has done for Fellini and for us during such a difficult time.

Despite the distance, her involvement has been absolute: always available, attentive, explaining every detail clearly and with impeccable professionalism. Her knowledge of feline medicine is impressive, but what truly makes the difference is her warm, humane, and empathetic approach, both with the cats and with the people who love them.

We have felt supported, heard, and cared for at all times. Elisa not only inspires confidence through her expertise but also calm and reassurance through her communication skills. It's clear she loves her work and deeply understands cats and their needs.

Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for your dedication, honesty, and sensitivity. Fellini has been in the best possible hands, even remotely. I wholeheartedly recommend her to anyone looking for an expert cat veterinarian and, above all, a truly great professional and an even better person.

We came to Barcelona five months ago with my cat, Pofuduk. I spent a month looking for a good veterinarian. We went to Clínica FELINA Barcelona because of my 11-year-old cat's eye discharge and joint problems. Dr. Diego treated us very well. He explained everything that needed to be done for Pofuduk's treatment, step by step. We were able to communicate in English, and the doctor treated him with great care. He performed his first maintenance appointment.

My cat and I left there happy and reassured. My cat's treatment will continue, perhaps for a long time; the important thing is that I feel confident, and we would like to choose this clinic again.

The clinic is clean and well-organized.

I would like to thank the receptionist and Dr. Diego.

For minor problems, it's a good place. They're almost always on time and treat the cats well.

The problem arises when your cat has to be hospitalized and spend the on-call hours there, when the staff is clearly insufficient. They don't have time to answer calls, allow visits to the admitted animals, or simply write in their medical records. If you love your cats and they're seriously ill, don't leave them there for a weekend. And this isn't a criticism of the on-call staff, but of the management and the center's operating model.

It's also not normal to decide to subject an animal with a suspected tumor and metastasis to major surgery involving an abdominal incision of more than 8 cm. No matter how many informed consent forms were signed or how well-planned the surgery was.

If the day before, blood work comes in—not discussed with the owners—showing that all three hematological lines are clearly affected (severe anemia and leukopenia with neutropenia), that animal will not be operated on. The person who made the decision to operate, based on that information, seemed more concerned with opening a wound and billing than with the animal's actual well-being.

Things took an even worse turn after the surgery, when we had to return our cat because she was leaking fluid from the wound, wasn't moving, and wasn't eating. Initially, the care was good, but my last memory of her was witnessing them insert a tube through her nose and sew it to her head.

The next day, we couldn't see her because of "overwork." They didn't even call us. For hours, they didn't even consider starting antibiotic treatment, despite the fact that the follow-up ultrasounds showed an increase in free abdominal fluid, with internal echoes and signs of organization—findings consistent with an exudate and not a simple post-surgical transudate. Treatment was started late, when her deterioration was already evident.

Hours passed without effective monitoring. Or at least that's what's reflected in her medical record, which I'll include screenshots of. Ultimately, she didn't make it past the fourth day of her hospital stay. And the last time we were able to be with her was, quite literally, to unknowingly torture her.

At no point was it hinted that she was in critical condition. At no point was a poor prognosis mentioned, nor was the possibility of letting her go.

One day, without warning, we received a phone call informing us of her death. The end.

I'm attaching a screenshot of her medical record showing the number of hours without any records or care.

I left a review during the worst of times, expressing my gratitude... in 2021... and in 2026, my gratitude remains strong, and I will always be thankful. I'm not from Barcelona, ​​so I don't have the opportunity to take my children to the clinic for appointments. I always go there to pick up medication for the mother of the three children who passed away; she also has leukemia. I continue to go to CFB to get her medication, and whenever I have a question, Salva is always there to help.

I will never be able to adequately thank him for the support he gave us when we said goodbye to our three children and for the continued help he provides so that Mom can have a good future and a good quality of life.

Thank you again, today and always.

———————-

I have nothing but praise for CFB and, above all, for Salvador Cervantes. I must say that I never knew the clinic director was treating us until I read it in his emails. It might seem silly, but to me it shows an incredible level of humility.

On July 14th, we received the worst news of 2021: one of our kittens was diagnosed with FELV, feline leukemia virus.
Our kitten was born at home; her mother arrived during the lockdown, and on May 9th, 2020, the three kittens were born. We decided to keep the family at home, microchipped them, neutered them, and vaccinated them—with all the vaccines, even for FELV. We thought they would be tested, but no, our vet didn't test them before vaccinating them.

That Wednesday, July 14th, they told us that one of the kittens was positive. They told me we could only wait for her to pass away. She wasn't moving her hind legs anymore. I know there's no cure, but I refused to do nothing and just wait. I've always volunteered with an animal shelter in Cáceres (Cristicats, thank you too!), and they recommended I talk to Salvador. I called, sent an email explaining everything, and on Saturday we were at the clinic. Salvador was very honest from the beginning. Very difficult months/years await you, as her mother has probably passed it on to her, and that's how we can say it is. My little Pompi couldn't move her back legs because she has lymphoma. Now she's receiving treatment, and although we know she might only be with us for a few months, she's getting the best quality of life we ​​can. Now she moves her legs a little more, gets on the sofa, eats on her own, and we've managed to help her gain weight.

No, they aren't treating her at CFB right now because I don't live in Barcelona, ​​and Salvador told me to keep things as simple as possible. What does this tell me again? That Salvador's only concern is that Pompi does well and that he wants to give her the best possible quality of life. They aren't treating her there, but a few days after I was at CFB, I received an email asking about her. What does that indicate again? We were not only treated by the best possible professional, but also by an incredible person who truly cares for them.

I can only thank you for your care, and especially you, Salva, for always being there, helping and advising me so that our little one can have the best possible quality of life for as long as she wants and we are lucky enough to share with her.

Thank you, THANK YOU for EVERYTHING ❤

A huge recommendation for this clinic. We took our cat in with a urinary tract obstruction. Maria, the veterinarian, diagnosed him immediately and treated him quickly and with great professionalism. He was discharged after two days.

Throughout the entire process, the veterinary team maintained constant communication with us (even on holidays!) and explained everything as clearly as possible, also in English, since our Spanish isn't very good. They even checked on him several days after we got home.

10/10 service. We are so lucky to have found this clinic.
Our cat decided to get sick on Christmas Day! He was treated with so much love and care, we'll see how he does. Thank you!

It's unacceptable that I call them for 3 days in a row to ask for a visit and they hang up AND don't even put you on hold. They hang you up directly or you listen to how they talk and from what you hear it seems unprofessional

We are super happy with Clínica Felina Barcelona. We arrived there a little desperate after going to 3 different vets. Our almost seven year old cat had chronic gingivostomatitis that caused him a lot of pain and stopped eating. Once diagnosed, they treated and operated on him and now he is recovering and much better. The treatment received is very good, the delicacy of how they took care of him and monitored him, the explanations given, the humane treatment with us, everything. They are very good professionals and they have already won us over as loyal customers. Thank you, Salvador, Anna, Marta, Elena and everyone who works at CFB.

I'm so glad we took our cats to this clinic. The service is cat-friendly; the vet is efficient, lovely, and has an incredibly gentle touch when giving vaccinations. Our cats were very well taken care of today at their appointment with Dr. Elisa. Thank you so much! ☺️

Great professionals. They have been very humane and clear with the diagnosis. Special thanks to Lidia for the treatment given at all times to both little Maui and the family and to Elisa the oncologist who has been attentive at all times. Thank you❤️

Both the vets and the assistants who cared for Luca made me feel like he was in the best hands. I feel like they treated him like he was their own cat, with so much love and patience. Luca will now continue his treatment at home, but I won't hesitate to take him back if necessary. Thank you!!

I only went in to ask about prices and it gave me a really bad feeling, a real bad feeling. That's why I started reading reviews and ugh, I wouldn't take my cats there for anything! My feeling was that they like easy money, and I see I wasn't wrong!

EDIT: A RESPONSE TO THE CLINIC'S ANSWER:
When they visit you, after explaining how sick your cat is, how he's been eating less and less over the months until he's not eating at all, you say he can't continue like this, and they tell you they can stabilize him. You think you could keep him for a few more days and don't mention euthanasia. Then they called and said his vital signs were better and even said they could do a biopsy, by puncturing his liver! They suggested we pick him up the next day to spend the weekend at home, and they would call on Monday to discuss how it went. I agreed.
Since we took him out of the carrier after two days (not one as they said), it was INHUMAN. I couldn't imagine it compared to how he was when he came into the clinic (independent). Knowing the state he was in, why did they say we could pick him up? Euthanasia should be proposed; I don't know how he is. Regarding your comment "I wanted to end by speaking generally about those who use social media to judge or harm," we have no intention of judging or harming: we have told the truth.

My daughter has already written a review about what happened to our 17-year-old cat, Leo, but I would like to share what I saw because I was the one who took him to the clinic. He had been eating less and less for months, and when we took him (as an emergency) on Thursday the 30th, he hadn't eaten anything for almost four days. He was skin and bones: he had gone from over 6 kg to over 3 kg and was very weak. We had already considered euthanasia at another clinic, where they refused, and at another clinic a year and a half ago, they found a problem with his liver, which they said could be a tumor. At Clínica Felina, where we went as an emergency, I told the vet how poorly he had been eating for months, less and less each time, and that he hadn't eaten for four days. She asked if he was vomiting and had diarrhea, which I confirmed, and I suppose she already suspected it was liver-related. He was dehydrated, and she said to admit him to stabilize him and try to get him to eat. Later, she called me and confirmed that his pulse and temperature were better, and that he could go home the next day to spend the weekend and see how he was doing. The next day, Friday, we went to pick him up, but they told us (without warning) that he wasn't well, that he was still dehydrated, and that he had to stay. On Saturday morning, a woman called saying that he was more active, that he had eaten three times (!!), about 40 grams of mousse, and that the doctor would call later. She called in the afternoon, saying curtly that we could come pick him up if we wanted, and when we asked if he was eating, he said no! Confused by the conflicting information about his food, we decided to go get him. When we arrived, they tried to give him some food, which he refused to lick, and I already had a bad feeling about it. When we got home and took him out of the carrier, we were horrified to see his condition. He was sitting on two diapers, one on top of the other, soaked with urine. His legs and bottom were completely wet and had a strange brownish color, as if something had been poured on them. We washed and dried him. The worst part was that he couldn't walk; his legs were paralyzed, and he was dragging himself along the floor. Obviously, he had been in the carrier with two diapers the entire time he was hospitalized: we had put the first one in. He was somewhat alert for about an hour and a half, then he became still and lethargic. He didn't eat. We went to bed, leaving him on the floor on a blanket. When we got up on Sunday before 8:00, he was completely stretched out on the floor, unable to move, whimpering, and he had peed. We called the feline clinic for urgent euthanasia, and the woman who answered said the vet wouldn't arrive until 8:30. (Aren't there any vets available at night for emergencies?)

I don't understand how they thought it was a good idea to send him home in this condition, and yet they should have suggested euthanasia much sooner when they saw he wasn't eating. In total, by Sunday he had gone almost seven days without a bite.

A disaster we can't get out of our heads.

ADDENDUM: Regarding the comment left on my review. If the only conclusion you draw is that we're trying to cause harm, then I see a lack of willingness to reflect. I don't doubt your commitment to animals. But in this whole affair, no one is taking responsibility for anything. The first clinic my parents went to isn't taking responsibility for not having checked the cat's medical history. You aren't taking responsibility for the cat's deteriorating condition. I'm not absolving my parents of responsibility either; they made poor decisions and were naive.

The comment is harsh, but it was even harder to see my cat suffer and cry for help (for some time now). All I ask is that 1) you don't discharge a terminally ill animal at night and 2) you don't prolong the unprolongable.

---

I'll be completely honest and clarify that I'm a third party. I have a physical disability, and it was my parents who took our cat to the clinic. But I did have to witness the poor animal suffering at home.

There's certainly a lesson here for both sides.

To the veterinary profession: please stop offering useless treatments to older and/or terminally ill animals (cats, in this case). You're only prolonging their suffering. Really, what's so scary about mentioning that euthanasia is an option when the animal is suffering and there's nothing else that can be done?

To pet owners: don't be fooled. We know when our pets are truly suffering, and when there's nothing more that can be done, we don't prolong it. It's never worth it.

Anyway, the recent case:

We took my 17-year-old cat, Leo, to the vet in very serious condition. They confirmed what we already knew: it was his liver, and there was no solution. They admitted him anyway.

The next day, they informed us that he was still not stable. A bad sign, but we were expecting it. We started considering euthanasia.

On the second day, they told us he was better, more active, and had eaten. Normal blood pressure, normal temperature, good hydration. We could take him home to see how he progressed. What condition was he in when they brought him back? Oh my God...

To begin with, they had put the cat in the carrier with diapers completely soaked in urine. In the two days he was hospitalized, they didn't clean him even once. (This is due to staff shortages. Diego, hire more people.)

Then, at home, his condition was clearly WORSE. He was somewhat alert for about an hour, but after that, he went downhill. He wouldn't eat anything and was practically paraplegic, dragging himself on the floor and unable to sleep. He deteriorated rapidly throughout the night, urinating on himself, and the next morning he was half DEAD. We rushed him back to the clinic to have him euthanized.

Their clinical assessment was very superficial. They returned him to us in a deplorable state. Just because an animal has its eyes open and/or its head raised doesn't mean it's okay—it's surviving. They forced Churu into its mouth to prove it was eating, even though the cat showed no interest.

A hellish ordeal and a huge sum of money, only to end up torturing the animal, and it's not the first time this has happened to us, here and elsewhere with other animals. As I said before, it seems to be a pattern.

I apologize for being so blunt, but I speak from the deepest sadness.
Very good care specializing in cats only

I called to request a house call from the vet, but the woman who answered told me they no longer make house calls and gave me the name of another veterinary clinic that was very good and would see me sooner. I don't understand why, since my cats are patients at this clinic, they have to give me a different vet. I would like to know if this veterinary clinic is closing. Thank you.

My cat Orson was a difficult cat in his early years, and it was hard to find a clinic that understood his behavioral challenges and could help me with his case. Years ago, the clinic provided invaluable assistance through their ethologist. In his later years, he always received excellent care and close monitoring of his health issues. He had to be hospitalized on more than one occasion, and the care he received was outstanding. Sadly, he didn't overcome his illness, as he was also elderly, but throughout the entire process of treatment, euthanasia, and everything else, the professionalism and compassion of everyone at the clinic made me feel confident that my cat was in the best hands. Thanks to their facilities, the moment of saying goodbye was very intimate and beautiful. Thank you for everything.

We took our cat Mixa to the emergency vet, and unfortunately, she arrived in very serious condition. We could only say goodbye to her, but I am incredibly grateful for the empathy, professionalism, and humanity shown to my son (she was his faithful companion until the very end) by the veterinarian who treated us.

Thank you 🫂

I thought I'd found an excellent clinic, but I've realized that's not the case. The doctors seem very friendly, and their public demeanor with the cats is fine, but I've noticed that they practically never actually solve the kittens' problems. Everything always ends with "We need to run tests." I have three cats, and I spend a considerable amount of money there almost every month on all the tests they always have to do, and the problem is never resolved! One of them is three years old and has had diarrhea with a little blood since the beginning. At first, he had irritable bowel syndrome, then parasites, then he was perfectly fine (but he was still passing blood), then he had parasites again, and now they're telling me he needs another stool test. And each time it costs €100-120, just for tests and to give him Fortiflora. I'm not a vet, but I have three cats at home who eat, drink, and defecate in the same place, and only one of them has a problem. And there they tell me, "He needs to be tested for parasites!" The second one is six years old and constantly has the flu, a cough, and a runny nose, and they never solve the problem. When he has a flare-up, they tell me I have to take him in urgently, giving me an appointment two days later, and then say, "He needs more tests."

I'm so sorry because I was actually fine with it at first, but I'm not going to take my three cats there anymore just for tests!

Thank you very much for the care, the tact and the support. For the sincerity in the diagnosis. Also for the speed of the attention, even though we had never visited with you.
It was a good place to say goodbye to Berta.
THANK YOU 🥰

I had taken my cats to the clinic on other occasions without any complaints.

Unfortunately, my last experience was very negative. From the emergency call, when I explained that my cat was behaving strangely, that he had been hiding for days and was losing his balance, they advised me to bring him in for an emergency appointment (which I didn't quite understand). When I arrived during "emergency" hours, I overheard the receptionist telling the veterinarian that I was bringing my cat in because he was hiding, nothing more. A veterinarian came to ask me if he was panting, to which I replied no. Since it was an emergency appointment, they made me go to a cubicle to wait. I peeked in and saw the team eating. They examined him, did blood tests and ultrasounds, and decided to admit him. For three days, they repeated ultrasounds; I had to keep calling the clinic to get updates. They discharged him with a diagnosis of "kidney problems." A few days later, at a follow-up appointment, I explained that the cat was still acting strangely and that I was worried about his loss of balance. He was then diagnosed with osteoarthritis in his hip (but not before repeating tests) and prescribed pain medication. I asked how long he would take the medication, but they didn't give me a time limit. When I told them I wasn't comfortable with the diagnosis, they said it could be something neurological, but they didn't have the equipment and recommended I go to a hospital. I had to insist several times to get them to send me the reports. The diagnosis at the first visit to the other clinic was clear: otitis media spreading to the brain with meningitis, but with suspicions of something more serious. Unfortunately, after further tests, the diagnosis was a tumor with no possibility of treatment, and a horrible end for Santi.
What I'm trying to say is, first, the initial care from reception is terrible. Second, if you're not sure about the diagnosis, don't wait to have several tests done and repeated.

I fully understand the incredibly hard work you do, but you should be a little more humble when referring cases without a clear diagnosis, before it's too late, as unfortunately has been the case here.

In my case, both with Ron and with the recently deceased Nebel, the treatment has been great, in Ron's case it's great with the medication and the monitoring that is done and in Nebel's case everything was tried until the end. Honestly, 10/10 for me.

Over 20 Years of Absolute Trust
For more than two decades, I've trusted Clínica Felina Barcelona to care for my cats, and I couldn't be more grateful for the treatment, ethics, and professionalism I've always received. I've been through all kinds of situations with my animals: routine checkups, complicated illnesses, very painful goodbyes… And I've always, always felt they were in the best possible hands.

It's truly saddening to read judgments or comments that take this team's work out of context, because I know—from my own consistent experience of over 20 years—that they act with impeccable ethics and profound respect, both for the animals and for the people who care for them.

At Clínica Felina Barcelona, ​​they not only care for the cats with knowledge and sensitivity, but they also support you as a human throughout the entire process. I've never felt rushed or treated like just another number. On the contrary: I've always found them listening, empathetic, and a genuine commitment to animal welfare.

For me, they're not just professionals: they're a team of people who love what they do and it shows in every consultation. And that, over time, is what matters most. Thank you for continuing to be there, with that dedication, even when you're not valued as you deserve.

Thank you Salva, Anna, Diego, Elisa, Marta, and the rest of the professionals who work with them.

A great place to take your cat, excellent service (they explain everything in detail, which is much appreciated), they call to keep you informed every step of the way, and, at least in my case, they demonstrated sound professional judgment both when performing diagnostic tests and after receiving the results, when deciding on the treatment. Thank you! Especially to Carla and Ana, the veterinarians who treated Charlie. It's a shame they returned him to me filthy, with his paws covered in sand and urine; their hygiene was definitely commendable, but that's about it.

Terrible experience at this clinic.

They claim to be an emergency clinic, and I was shocked when they told me they don't have an ultrasound machine. They performed blood work, including biochemistry, and a physical exam. They gave him an IV drip and scheduled an appointment for this week for an ultrasound to rule out a possible tumor.

This morning my cat was much worse. His vet examined him and found he has pneumonia. They performed an ultrasound and X-rays to rule out a possible tumor, and thankfully everything is fine (I was so nervous I almost thought he had a tumor). This morning I called the Felina Barcelona clinic requesting the blood work results so I could show them to the vet and avoid having to test my cat again, but they haven't sent them.

This afternoon, with my cat now stable, I managed to speak with one of the managers, who very proudly told me that they do have an ultrasound machine; The reason the ultrasound wasn't performed was because "the staff in the emergency room don't have enough experience with ultrasounds," and they didn't do it "because they're not going to charge for a test they don't know how to do." They said "they should have called someone with experience to come to the clinic and do it" (what's ideal in an emergency? - waiting). "That was the mistake they made" (having less experienced staff in the emergency room is also quite logical! Because it's the service where you have the most time to react, and the less knowledge you have, the easier it is to act, even to rule things out!).

After the manager explained the clinic's procedures to me in great detail, I admitted to recording the call so I could file a complaint and requested a refund for the visit, since, as she herself acknowledged, you can't charge for a job you don't know how to do. Did they refund my money? Yes, but I don't recommend that any cat enter this clinic during emergency hours. It may be an isolated incident, but they are living beings, and just like humans, they need qualified professionals in emergency services. Just as in human healthcare, we must report these kinds of situations so they stop happening.

A very good clinic. We took our cat Gandhi there until he passed away from kidney failure, and now we take Henry there. They offer one hour of free parking. They treat the animals and their families very well. We are extremely grateful, especially Diego.

Super happy with all of you, my Nika is doing very well after coming to your house; she had a hard time with the tests and the medication for so long but it was worth it. Marta has been very attentive to her and me to keep me informed at all times. How lucky to find professionals and people who love the mixis so much....thank you very much!!!
If you are going outside normal hours, remember to call and ring the bell on the wall at the entrance on the left.

I have nothing but words of gratitude for them.
Yesterday we took Merlin for a second opinion for the first time... he had been very sick for two weeks, and after taking him to other veterinary clinics, having tests done, and making the poor thing miserable, the best thing we could do for him was to bring him to you.
He is now at peace because there was nothing more that could be done, and we are so grateful that you didn't do any more tests, saving us from wasting money and, above all, from making him suffer.

Thank you for your empathy and professionalism... our last moments with Merlin were very difficult but also very, very beautiful, thanks to Anna's help... thank you so much.

She died at the clinic. My kitten got very sick, and we took her to this clinic because they knew her there and had saved her five years ago. That's true. But that time they didn't sedate her for tests. This time, though, they sedated her, and she couldn't handle it. It's such a shame. Why don't veterinarians try to avoid sedation at all costs when it's possible? Don't accept sedation when there's even the slightest chance of avoiding it. Many animals in a delicate state can't survive it. It's such a pity I couldn't see my kitten in her final moments... I was away (I was going to return the next day), and my partner took her to the vet. We agreed to everything the vet told us, and in the end, we brought her back from the clinic already dead. I'm sure that if I had waited one more day before taking her to the clinic, I would have seen her alive.
Thank you for your attention. You saved our lives. Thank you to Andreina and Ana Pallares.
Many thanks to the entire team at the Clinica Felina, we had Bastet, our 18-year-old senior, admitted, for a few days and as always, the patient treatment towards us, and especially towards her.

I've been taking my asthmatic kitten to this clinic for a while now, and I couldn't be more grateful to the team. From the very first visit, the treatment has been impeccable: kind, patient, and always attentive to both my pet and me. It's clear they truly love what they do and that the animals' well-being is their priority.

They've been very thorough at every checkup, explaining everything clearly and always giving me peace of mind that Dibu is in the best hands. In addition, the facilities are clean, organized, and well-equipped.

It's such a relief to know I have such wonderful professionals!

Thank you so much for caring for Winita with such love and dedication. You are a wonderful team, with great compassion and sensitivity towards animals. (Elena, Lidia, Elisa, Judith...)

I couldn't have chosen better professionals.

You were instrumental in improving Winita's health and quality of life until her very last moments; I'm sure she was grateful to you as well.

The support you provided to the family, the respect shown during the loss of a loved one, and the respect shown to the animal clearly demonstrate the clinic's values.

After taking my cats there a few times, I stopped. I didn't like how they were treated. For example, they did scouring. Lots of tests without giving any diagnosis… It felt like they were just trying to charge for procedures instead of helping the animal.

They returned my cat to me half-dead! They gave him to me in the carrier without even telling me. When I got home, I realized the poor animal couldn't even hold his head up. They probably used him for blood transfusions. These people have no ethics! Don't go there!

We have been treated by 10, which is what a veterinary center should be. Professionals who love animals, who give careful explanations and are not simply a business so that their patients, our feline companions, are well.
Fantastic clinic. Everyone is very kind and professional. You're leaving your cat in good hands. I highly recommend it!

My experience, despite not having a happy ending, has been more bearable thanks to the treatment and humanity that they have transmitted to me.
Diego...unsurpassed, Roma could not have been in better hands, the star of the month that is in the sky today is Roma, who will always be in our hearts. Shine bright princess
Dr. Diego does whatever he wants with Mia; she always feels calm and comfortable, and they keep us very well informed about everything. We are so grateful for everything ❤️ 100% recommended

Everything was excellent. We had my kitten operated on by them—a tooth extraction—and I truly received professionalism and genuine concern for her recovery.

I trusted them and will continue to trust them for future consultations for my pets, and I wholeheartedly recommend that you go to them if you have a problem because they care for your pet as if it were their own.

Thank you for everything!

On January 23rd, I took my cat Thais to the Feline Clinic because she was experiencing nausea and occasional vomiting.
At the Feline Clinic, they ran more tests and suspected IBD or intestinal lymphoma, recommending an intestinal biopsy for confirmation.
The biopsy began at 10:00 AM on January 24th. An hour later, they called me: Thais wasn't breathing well and had a pleural effusion. They drained fluid and told me there were no tumor cells, no signs of heart disease, and no pancreatitis. Even so, they insisted it could be a "diffuse tumor." They performed a thoracic ultrasound but also didn't find any tumor.
After the surgery, Thais wasn't responding well. She was disoriented and weak, but they assured me this was normal due to the anesthesia.
At 4:00 AM on Saturday, they called me: fluid had accumulated in her lungs again, and they sedated her to drain it once more. When I went to see her in the morning, she was still unresponsive, and the assistant suggested euthanasia. I couldn't believe it.

The vet told me that older cats have trouble coming out of anesthesia and that Thias was probably like that because of a tumor (which they couldn't find). She also said that sometimes, very skittish cats experience a kind of traumatic shock due to the surgical stress and being taken out of their comfort zone. We discussed the possibility of taking her home so she could recover in her own environment, since Thais was a very timid cat. She wouldn't let anyone touch her except me, she had never been hospitalized, and her comfort zone was my bedroom. When we got home, I put her on the bed. She purred, but she was still ataxia.

On Sunday, Thais was in better spirits because she had been purring and had eaten the baby food I had given her, but she was still ataxia and weak. The vet told me it was normal, and to be patient because Thais was in a bad state. I didn't understand what she meant by "bad state," because before going to the clinic, my cat had been nauseous and sometimes vomited undigested food, and she had left the clinic in terrible condition, unable to stand.

On Monday, I called her again to ask why they hadn't prescribed antibiotics. She said that if the wound wasn't red, they weren't necessary. At that moment, I thought about how it had been surgery and there could be an internal infection. I also mentioned that Thais wasn't blinking and already had keratitis due to dry eye, but they didn't prescribe eye drops either.

On Tuesday, I decided to take her to the vet in Premià because Thais was still the same. The first thing the vet did was draw blood to check her kidneys. She told me that when a cat isn't recovering well from anesthesia, that's the first thing they check.

The diagnosis was devastating: Thais had kidney failure and a severe internal infection, and she ultimately died in my arms.
The next day, the feline clinic called with the biopsy results: Thais had low-grade lymphoma, treatable with medication and with a good prognosis.
They didn't do any post-operative blood work before discharging her. They focused on a large, diffuse tumor and her age, giving her no hope and ignoring the fact that Thais had an internal infection and progressive kidney failure.
I requested her post-surgery blood work, and they sent me the pre-operative results. They told me that when they gave them to me, they didn't see any signs of infection or kidney failure because the urine readings and specific gravity were normal, and that kidney failure can have a wide range of diagnoses and can present as a sudden process in a short period of time. I don't know if Thais left the clinic with kidney failure or not, but what is certain is that they didn't perform any blood tests before discharging her to check her condition and assess any potential post-surgical complications.
The feline clinic gave my cat a terminal diagnosis because of her age of 16 and because they were convinced she had a large, diffuse tumor that they couldn't find. Meanwhile, Thais had an internal infection and kidney failure that they neither detected nor treated.
Thais spent her last days in agony while I believed it was just the effect of the anesthesia.

It's been over a year and I still need to express my gratitude to this clinic. Everything would have been very different if we had known it before. We were desperate and a friend told us that it was the best clinic in Catalonia for cats.
We had been going to the vet for months without a good diagnosis, constantly, and finally Tesla had a serious kidney problem; here, in twenty minutes and after four tests that were done immediately, they clearly explained the situation to us, including the cause of the kidney failure.
I don't want to talk about the other clinics, but I know that Tesla wouldn't be with us today if we hadn't come here.
Feline kidney failure is a common disease, and if anyone has a kitten in this situation and reads these lines, I recommend this clinic with all my heart. Because I think about what they might be going through, because we were literally told in other places that it was impossible for him to recover (I can't forget that someone told us "you'll have to make a decision").
We know that the disease cannot be cured and that it is taking its course, but Marta Miralpeix, and all the professionals who have attended to us, have been teaching us everything we can do so that he has the best quality of life possible. Marta has known from day one what medications he has been needing and has taught us to identify the symptoms to recognize if something is wrong.
It hurts me to read some negative reviews that I consider very unfair. I know from experience, to my shame, that when pain does not allow us to reason, we can end up blaming those who are doing the impossible to save the life of the one we love so much. A negative review can hurt a lot, and I cannot remain silent after reading some things, because the experience I have had in the last thirteen months tells me that a cat cannot be in better hands. This clinic is the only place where I have known what professional excellence is.
An infinite hug to the whole team, especially to Marta Miralpeix.

We went with my blind father and his guide dog to look for some pills for my cat and the girl at the reception refused us entry, when they should know that a guide dog can enter any establishment, and this information is collected (take a look at it, it will be good for you to be informed, please) in law 19/2009, of November 26, on access to the environment of people accompanied by assistance dogs, specifically in articles 11 and 12 where it specifically talks about the Determination of places, premises, establishments, accommodation, transport and public or public use spaces. For your information, a guide dog can ONLY enter two places: an operating room and an establishment and factories/establishments where raw food is handled. What you did is an exclusion of a person and, moreover, without giving any coherent explanation, all you did was smile and say no, I'm sorry... Don't take your animals to a place that doesn't love or value animals or has no knowledge of them!!!! Whether they are cats, dogs or parakeets!!! And we won't report you to the guide dog foundation because we won't waste time!!! Good luck
